newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Capitalbank to hike capital to 12 bln lvs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Capitalbank to hike capital to 12 bln lvs.

text.p: Bulgaria's private Capitalbank decided to raise its share capital to 12 billion levs from 1.4 billion levs through a new rights issue, the bank's board chairman said on Wednesday.

"Capitalbank shareholders voted to raise capital to 12 billion levs through a new share issue. It will be distributed only among current shareholders in proportion to their stakes," Angel Parvanov told Reuters.
Existing shareholders will be invited to subscribe to the new shares.

Bulgaria's First Financial Company owns 47 percent of Capitalbank. Bulgaria's state-owned Teraton and Russia's Royalflesh have 25 percent each and the remaining three percent are held by another Russian firm, Rontadent.

By increasing its capital, the bank would improve its capital to risk assets ratio, which is currently negative. Its more than $20 million of overdue debt forms part of its assets, worsening its capital adequacy.
Bankers say that in its present state it could not operate under a currency board regime due to be introduced in June.
The bank could survive and pay its dues to the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) and commercial banks totalling some $7 million if it succeeds to collect at least part of the $20 million, Parvanov said.
"Now time is running out for Capitalbank and if its debtors do not resume payments, we will take an adequate decision concerning the bank," a BNB official who declined to be named told Reuters.
Capitalbank's debt to the BNB alone totalled $3.5 million as of December 30, 1996, BNB figures showed.
The capital increase is in line with BNB plans to amend its regulations and raise limits for banks' minimum capital.
Minimum capital requirements at present are set at 1.4 billion levs for a domestic banking licence and at 2.2 billion for a full licence. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 8569; 981 4145
